Read at `step-plan`, `test-spec`, `test` and `document`, and when a test gate refuses. ## Test loop `step-plan` records the work item\'s test command list in its result: `"test_commands": [{"command": "<shell command>", "suite": "focused" | "regression" | "check", "ids": ["TC-9"], "min_tests": 1}]` (`ids` and `min_tests` optional, and never on a `check` row). It also records `"paths"` (the repository-relative files or globs the item will change) and `"steps": [{"id": "S1", "task": "...", "deps": []}]`: every implementation step in order, each step\'s actual prerequisites as earlier step IDs in `deps` (`[]` for an independent step; order alone does not imply dependency). ShipLoop refuses a done `step-plan` without any of these; an empty command list needs `test_commands_na` with the reason, and a list with no `check` row (lint, type or build) needs `check_na`. A regression command marked `"minimum": true` runs at every step, an unmarked one at the item\'s last step only; a plan of two or more steps marks one or gives `minimum_na` ([what each step runs](testing-and-documentation.md#what-each-step-runs)). The `test` stage follows `implement`. Tests are written after the build phase and must assert the behaviour the test spec\'s oracle states; ShipLoop mutates a sample of the item\'s changed product lines and refuses each surviving mutant that no focused test kills and no `mutant_dispositions` entry explains.
